clue.text: Be unexpectedly helpful and arrive with seats on time

indicators.note: the seats come with the time letter held among them, sitting on top of it at the front

blocks.note: to turn up is to arrive
T is the abbreviation for time
rumps are what we sit on

explanation.surface: Someone shows up punctually bringing chairs for everyone, a pleasant surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The seats are bottoms, not chairs: RUMPS placed on T, after TURN UP, gives TURN UP TRUMPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up trumps is an idiom for producing a better result than expected or proving useful.

clue.text: Handy accessories in suites when struggling with onset of sniffles?

indicators.note: letters that are struggling are thrashing about out of their order
the onset of a word is its very beginning, so just its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of sniffles

explanation.surface: A hotel guest with a cold is glad of handy hankies in their suite.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper tissues are kept to hand, literally handy accessories for blowing a nose.

clue.text: E.g. party regularly cheers after runs in sporting event

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at a steady interval, here every second one
after tells us the runs letter goes first and the rest follow it

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written, without the dots
the second and fourth letters of party
ta is an informal British thank you

explanation.surface: A boating party celebrates with cheers at a sporting occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting of boat races, so a sporting event.

clue.text: Greatest State majority

blocks.note: to state something is to utter it
most means the greater part

explanation.surface: Reads like a headline about the largest majority won in a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a noun, as in a US state, but it is the verb meaning to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttermost means extreme, of the furthest or greatest degree.

clue.text: Upright, somewhat sophisticated and silent

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following word is used
in a down entry, upright means written going up, so bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters inside the word

explanation.surface: A description of a poised, refined, quiet person.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken, understood without being said aloud.

clue.text: In Bordeaux, one bottle put out

blocks.note: un is French for one
bottle is British slang for courage

explanation.surface: A wine bottle opened in Bordeaux is set out on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is not wine but courage, as in losing your bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve someone is to unsettle them, and to put someone out is likewise to disconcert them.

clue.text: Motto of old pirate (British) south of Portugal

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of puts what follows above, so the Portugal letter comes first

blocks.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
rover is an archaic word for a pirate
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: The motto of an old British pirate who sailed off Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a short saying of wisdom, close in sense to a motto.

clue.text: So a detective's tampered with recording …

indicators.note: something tampered with has been interfered with and altered from its original arrangement

blocks.note: every letter, including the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A detective has doctored a piece of recorded evidence, the plot continuing into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A video cassette is a tape holding a recording of pictures and sound.

clue.text: … telephoned by a criminal? Unacceptable

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the detective was phoned by a crook, which is outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond the pale is an idiom for conduct outside the bounds of decency.

clue.text: Grasp popular model outside Grand Hotel

indicators.note: outside means one word goes round the others, enclosing them

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
to sit for a portrait is to model
G is short for grand, a thousand
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A popular fashion model stands outside a grand hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is understanding, a grasp of something as a noun.

clue.text: Excuse fellow wearing plastic bollard

indicators.note: the fellow is wearing the bollard, so it goes round him like clothing

blocks.note: a traffic cone is a plastic bollard
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Forgive a man who has put a traffic cone on his head, a familiar drunken prank.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to overlook or forgive an offence, a synonym of excuse as a verb.

clue.text: Line on map not quite identical to river

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls a little short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: identical in amount or value
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A line on a map is nearly the same as the river it follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is the imaginary line drawn on maps round the middle of the earth.

clue.text: Overrode protests about concealing missile

indicators.note: the two words are concealing the answer within their joined letters
about means turned round, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the run spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An official overruled objections and kept quiet about a missile.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile.

clue.text: Rib good person in coat that's a little short

indicators.note: a coat a little short has had its final letter trimmed off
in places the good person inside the coat

blocks.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: Tease a well-behaved man for wearing a coat that is too short.
explanation.walkthrough: Rib looks like a verb meaning tease, but it is the noun, the bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa is the anatomical Latin term for a rib.

clue.text: Source of seafood stored by cooks around end of June

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
cooks means the letters are worked over and mixed like ingredients
around places the mixed letters round the single letter from June

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of June

explanation.surface: Seafood kept by chefs through to the end of June.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster bed is a place on the seabed where oysters grow, a source of shellfish.

clue.text: Song and dance career that's not to be sniffed at!

definitions.text: that's not to be sniffed at!

blocks.note: making a song and dance is making a stink, a fuss
to career or bomb along is to move at speed

explanation.surface: A showbiz career in song and dance, praised as not to be sniffed at.
explanation.walkthrough: Career is the verb, to rush along, not a profession. The definition plays on the idiom: a stink bomb is literally something you would not want to sniff.
explanation.definitionFit: A stink bomb releases a foul smell, so it is literally not to be sniffed at, twisting an idiom meaning impressive.

clue.text: Pasta: it gets chap with no starter excited

indicators.note: with no starter means the first letter is dropped
excited letters are stirred up and jump out of their places

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man gets thrilled by pasta, especially when he has skipped the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter looks like a first course at the meal, but it means the first letter of chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a kind of pasta in long thin strands; the example stands for its category.

clue.text: Artist's studio Sartre claimed occasionally, right?

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter is used

blocks.note: the even letters across both words
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Questioning whether the philosopher Sartre said he worked in an artist's studio.
explanation.definitionFit: Atelier is the French word, used in English, for an artist's or designer's workshop.

clue.text: Inspire judge to catch up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a judge hears a case
to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: Encourage a judge to keep up with the case.
explanation.walkthrough: Catch up looks like a phrasal verb, but up is the reversal signal on catch alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten is to encourage, giving someone heart, close to inspire.

clue.text: Cut large tree on sierra

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another sits after it, so sierra comes first

blocks.note: S is sierra in the phonetic alphabet
L is the abbreviation for large
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Felling a big tree on a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: Sierra looks like a mountain range but is S in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A slash is a long cut, and to slash is to cut violently.

clue.text: Maybe Garfunkel article is tipping another singer

indicators.note: tipping turns the line over, so its letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Art Garfunkel, the singer of Simon and Garfunkel
an is the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps Art Garfunkel is the tip for a story on another singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Garfunkel stands for his first name, Art; that is why Maybe is there.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was a famous singer, so another singer besides Garfunkel.

clue.text: Remorseful, like journalist undermining bad actor

indicators.note: in a down entry, a word undermining another sits beneath it, so it comes last

blocks.note: as means like
a ham is an over-acting performer
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A sorry reporter who has undercut an overacting performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashamed means feeling guilt or shame, a synonym of remorseful.

clue.text: Observer husband spotted lying around in rubbish

indicators.note: lying around means turned about, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: an eye is what observes
H is the abbreviation for husband
spotted means saw

explanation.surface: A watcher spots a husband lounging about amid the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Observer looks like a person, or the newspaper, but it is simply the organ that observes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for nonsense or humbug, meaning rubbish as talk.

clue.text: Wading bird is there scratching wings and leg

indicators.note: scratching the wings means crossing out the letters at both edges of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
on, or leg, is the cricket side on which the batsman stands

explanation.surface: A wading bird stands there scratching its wings and leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side and on side are the same half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged bird that wades in shallow water to fish.

clue.text: Trendy mum taken by half of kipper ties

indicators.note: half of means only the first three of the six letters survive
taken by means held inside, so the trendy mum letters go inside

blocks.note: taken as written
in means fashionable
mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A fashionable mother wearing kipper ties, the wide ties of the 1970s.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum is not a mother but the word for silent, as in keep mum. A kipper tie is a very wide necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinship is family relationship, the ties that bind relatives.

clue.text: With little hesitation, fool finally bought old website

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: a twit is a fool
the last letter of bought
er is the brief sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A fool, barely pausing, bought an old website.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitter was the social media site renamed X in 2023, so it is the old name of a website.

clue.text: Best old friend embracing Henman perhaps

indicators.note: the friend is embracing, wrapping arms round, what follows

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a pal is a friend
Tim Henman, the British tennis player; perhaps marks him as one example of a Tim

explanation.surface: An old friend hugs the tennis player Tim Henman, his best mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal means the most favourable, the best possible.

clue.text: Support for the evening?

blocks.note: surface reading: something that holds you up on a night out
setter's reading: evening is making things even, flattening creases in clothes

explanation.walkthrough: Evening suggests night time, but read it as even-ing: smoothing out. The board supports clothes while they are pressed flat.
explanation.definitionFit: This household stand is the support on which clothes are smoothed flat, made even.
